evades_obstructions.obstruction: DH/Epstein filter (functional equation + explicit formula + L2 means hold, RH false)
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope, stated honestly: this route claims improved proportions on average over families, never full RH. It nonetheless interacts correctly with the filter: Davenport-Heilbronn-type objects have -F'/F coefficients with sum |c(n)|^2 ~ x^{1+delta}, so the averaged diagonal (T/pi) sum Lambda(n)^2 n^{-1} g(log n) blows up and the certificate is empty for them (paper Remark 7.2(iii) last sentence); and DH functions do not form an orthogonal family {chi mod q}, so the orthogonality step that replaces Montgomery-Vaughan has no DH analogue. The mechanism consumes Euler-product-derived coefficients Lambda(n)chi(n) with |coefficients| = Lambda(n) (Ramanujan trivially) plus family orthogonality - inputs the RH-false controls violate - but the output is still a lower-bound certificate insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros, so no RH claim is made.

evades_obstructions.how: That cap presumes the second-moment constant 1/lambda + lambda/3, i.e. form factor |alpha| at ALL frequencies (Poissonian growth). evades_obstructions.obstruction: Rodgers-Tao Lambda >= 0 (no sub-critical margin)
evades_obstructions.how: Binding for sub-direction (ii) and honestly absorbed: differentiation of xi is a smoothing (heat-flow-like) operation, so Lambda >= 0 means results about xi^(k) can NEVER be pulled back to xi/zeta by any un-smoothing bootstrap; moreover Conrey (1983) already gets on-line proportion -> 1 for xi^(k) unconditionally, confirming that 'proportion -> 1 as k -> infinity' carries no RH content. result.first_theorem: THEOREM F1 (family-averaged two-thirds at polylogarithmic height). For every delta in (0,1] there exist effective A = A(delta) <= 2+2delta, C(delta) and q0(delta) such that for all primes q >= q0 and all T with (log q)^A <= T <= q^{1/loglog q}: sum over chi mod q, chi != chi0 of N0s_chi(T,2T] >= (2/3 - C/loglog q) * sum over chi != chi0 of N_chi(T,2T], and likewise sum N_{d,chi} >= (5/6 - C/loglog q) sum N_chi; with the Montgomery-Taylor window cos(sqrt(2)Lambda s), the constants improve to 2 - 1/c1* = 0.67250... and 0.83625... . (Corollary via Markov: for every x in [0,1], the fraction of characters chi with N0s_chi >= x*N_chi is at least (2/3 - o(1) - x)/(1-x); e.g. half of all characters have a third of their zeros simple-and-on-line at height polylog q.) STATUS OF INPUTS: (1) per-character explicit formula, zero-side block decomposition, Lemma R, and assembly - all proven AND formalized (ThmE pipeline, ZeroConfig, RankTraceMult, count_certificate parametric in kappa); (2) orthogonality of characters, uniform RvM N_chi(t+1)-N_chi(t) << log(q(t+3)), Stirling for mu_chi - classical; (3) the Ingham taper lemma T0 - elementary classical analysis, construction exhibited above (product of sincs), needs only careful constants; (4) the family-averaged moment computation - elementary given (3), since orthogonality makes the off-diagonal vanish IDENTICALLY for X < q and all remaining errors are trivial bounds (chi0-removal << L*sqrt(X) per family; dual terms << L^2*X/q). result.mechanism:
THE CORE OBSERVATION. The entire Zeta23 certificate is linear in the two matrix moments: Lemma R at c=2 gives, per L-function, s1 >= 4 tr Ahat - ||Ahat||_F^2 - 2N, and tr and ||.||_F^2 are additive over block-diagonal direct sums. So for ANY finite family F of L-functions the certificate applies verbatim to the direct sum matrix DirectSum_{chi in F} Ghat_chi: sum_chi s1(chi) >= 4 sum_chi tr Ghat_chi - sum_chi ||Ghat_chi||_F^2 - 2 sum_chi N_chi. Averaging is therefore free on the zero side and the linear algebra; ALL new work is on the prime side, where the family average is computed by orthogonality instead of the Montgomery-Vaughan absolute-value bound. This changes which off-diagonal prime pairs must be controlled, and that is the entire game.

SUB-DIRECTION (i), TIER 1 - chi-AVERAGE AT FIXED PRIME q, T = polylog(q). Setup: for each chi != chi0 mod q (q prime, so all nonprincipal chi primitive), the paper's Theorem-E machinery gives the Weil form W_chi(f,g) = sum_rho m_rho h_f(gamma_rho) h_g(gamma_rho) with density nu_{X,chi} = mu_chi + P_{X,chi}, P_{X,chi}(tau) = -(1/pi) Re sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) chi(n) n^{-1/2-i tau}. Gabor grid tau_k = T + 2 pi k/L, k < d = floor(LT/2pi), L = Lambda * l_q, l_q := log(qT/2pi), X = e^L = (qT/2pi)^Lambda. Per-character zero side (formalized, arithmetic-free): Ahat_chi = P_chi + Q_chi, rank P_chi <= s1+s2, tr P_chi <= N_on, n_+(Q_chi) <= p, regardless of q,T.

First moment averaged: sum_{chi != chi0} tr Gtilde_chi = phi(q) a L Nbar (1+o(1)) with Nbar = (T/2pi) l_q, because (a) the mu_chi term is deterministic (Stirling, uniform in q), (b) sum_chi chi(n) = phi(q) 1_{n == 1 mod q} and n <= X < q forces n=1 (no prime-power terms AT ALL), (c) removing chi0 costs one character's trivial bound << L sqrt(X) = o(phi(q) T l_q). Second moment averaged: expanding P_{X,chi}(tau) P_{X,chi}(tau') produces chi(n)chibar(m)-terms and chi(n)chi(m)-terms. Orthogonality: sum_chi chi(n)chibar(m) = phi(q) 1_{n == m mod q}; for n,m <= X < q this forces n = m - THE OFF-DIAGONAL VANISHES IDENTICALLY. No Montgomery-Vaughan, no cancellation argument, nothing: the binding constraint X <= T^{1-eps} of the t-aspect is replaced by X < q, i.e. normalized bandwidth Lambda* = log q/log(qT) -> 1 when T = q^{o(1)}. The dual terms (nm == 1 mod q, nm = 1 + jq <= X^2) are bounded trivially by L^2 X/q = L^2 (qT)^Lambda / q -> 0 for Lambda <= 1 - 1/loglog q (even this close to 1, X/q <= e^{-log q/loglog q} T beats every polylog). Hence sum_{chi != chi0} tr Gtilde_chi^2 = phi(q) (T L/2pi)(l_q^2 + L^2/3)(1+o(1)), i.e. the averaged kappa is EXACTLY the paper's kappa(Lambda) = 1/Lambda + Lambda/3 -> 4/3, and the averaged certificate gives H(Lambda) -> 2/3 simple-and-on-line, 5/6 distinct, on average over the family - with T only polylog(q).

THE NAMED MISSING PIECE - THE TAPER (designed here). At T = polylog(q) the paper's Prop 4.2 dies: theta_0 ~ X^{1/2} log(4T)/D0^2 with X^{1/2} = (qT)^{Lambda/2} = q^{Lambda/2 + o(1)} while D0 <= T = polylog(q). The X^{1/2} = e^{L sup|Im gamma|} factor is unavoidable (zeros can be anywhere in the strip); what must improve is the REAL-AXIS decay of phihat: the C^3 ramp's r^{-2} is hopeless; we need near-exponential decay from a compactly supported window. Paley-Wiener forbids exp(-c|r|); Gevrey-s tapers give exp(-c|r|^{1/s}); the OPTIMAL choice is an Ingham taper: phi = 1_{[-(L-w)/2,(L-w)/2]} star psi, psi = star-product over j >= 1 of (2w_j)^{-1} 1_{[-w_j, w_j]}, with widths w_j = c_delta * w/(j (log(j+2))^{1+delta}), sum w_j = w/2, w = 1 fixed. Then phihat(z) = 2 sin((L-w)z/2)/z * prod_j sinc(w_j z), supp phi = [-L/2, L/2] exactly, phi = 1 on the middle, and the elementary bounds |sin(w(r-iy))| <= e^{w|y|}, |sinc(w_j(r-iy))| <= e^{w_j|y|} min(1, 1/(w_j|r|)) multiply to TAPER LEMMA T0: |phihat(r-iy)| <= C_delta e^{|y|L/2} exp(-|r|/(C_delta (1+log_+|r|)^{1+delta})) for all real r, |y| <= 1/2 (Ingham's criterion integral of eps(t)/t dt < infinity is exactly what permits eps(r) = c/(log r)^{1+delta}). Tail estimate with T0: with D0 = T/loglog q, ||E_chi|| <= sum_{gamma notin I'} m_rho ||u_rho||^2 <= C e^{L/2} * log(q) * exp(-2 c D0/(log D0)^{1+delta}) * (zero-density factor), which is o(1/q) as soon as T/(log T)^{1+delta} >= C' Lambda log q loglog q, i.e. T >= (log q)^{1+delta'} for any delta' > delta. The same near-exponential decay also repairs every window-restriction error in the Section 5 reduction (the sqrt(X)-pointwise bound on P_X now meets exp(-cD0/(log D0)^{1+delta}) instead of D0^{-2}), which is why the whole prime side re-runs at tiny T. This T0 is the single new analytic lemma; everything else is bookkeeping against the existing formalized pipeline.

Boundary bookkeeping: N_II (zeros in the D0-collars) << phi(q) D0 l_q = o(phi(q) T l_q) since D0 = T/loglog q; per-character RvM error O(log qT) sums to phi(q) O(log q) = o(phi(q) T l_q) since T -> infinity. Grid dimension d = floor(LT/2pi) = Lambda Nbar (1+o(1)) since log T/l_q -> 0. All checks pass; assembly gives F1 below.

TIER 2 - THE OZLUK REGIME (horizon of (i)): average ALSO over moduli q ~ Q (smooth weight). Now sum over q of phi(q) 1_{n == m mod q} converts the off-diagonal n - m = jq into averaged shifted convolutions sum_j sum_q w(q/Q) Lambda(n) Lambda(n+jq) - evaluable UNCONDITIONALLY by dispersion/asymptotic-large-sieve technology (Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan) for X up to Q^{2-eps}: effective bandwidth Lambda* = 2. The averaged second-moment constant becomes kappa_fam(Lambda) = 1/Lambda + (Lambda - 2/3 + (Lambda-1)^2)/Lambda^2 for 1 <= Lambda <= 2 (form factor |alpha| on [0,1], plateau 1 on [1,Lambda]); at Lambda = 2: kappa_fam = 13/12, certificate 2 - 13/12 = 11/12 = 0.91667 simple-and-on-line, (3-13/12)/2 = 23/24 distinct, ON AVERAGE - exactly Ozluk's GRH-conditional 11/12 with GRH removed by the rank-trace mechanism (the same de-conditionalization the paper performed on Montgomery). The Lean assembly consumes the new kappa with zero formal change (count_certificate is parametric in kappa). The window re-optimization at Lambda = 2 is a new variational problem: maximize Lambda (int v)^2/(int v^2 + int int K_2(Lambda(s-s')) v v) where K_2 is the kernel whose second derivative reproduces the plateau'd form factor; the Euler-Lagrange equation is a linear second-order integro-differential equation with piecewise-polynomial kernel - explicitly solvable (cosine on the bulk matched across the |alpha| = 1 breakpoint), expected to push 11/12 to ~0.92+.

SUB-DIRECTION (ii) - DERIVATIVE ESCALATION (designed, subordinate). Per-derivative transfer: Gauss-Lucas for genus-1 real entire functions puts all zeros of xi^{(k)} in the closed strip unconditionally (induction from xi; the paper's k=1 open-strip and Re xi'/xi > 0 arguments extend by the same Laguerre-type induction). The XiPrime/Transfer coefficient system generalizes: the prime side of the xi^{(k)} form carries Lambda(n) times polynomial weights in (log n)/l, still bandwidth-1 evaluable by the identical MV step; the second-moment constant kappa_k(lambda) is computable in closed form from the FGL-type form-factor recursion (k=1 is formalized). The xi'-VARIATIONAL PROBLEM (replacing the ad hoc quartic window): the functional is c^{(1)}(v) = lambda (int v)^2/(int v^2 + lambda^2 int int K^{(1)}(s-s') v v) with K^{(1)} the xi'-two-point kernel = |x| plus explicit lower-order polynomial corrections from the FGL density; differentiating the Euler-Lagrange identity twice yields a constant-coefficient linear ODE of order 2 or 4 (v'' + 2 lambda^2 (a_1 v + b_1 v'') = const), whose solutions are cos/cosh combinations - a closed-form optimizer replacing 0.86864 by an exact constant (predicted 0.870-0.875, below the RH-conditional 0.8825). k -> infinity: kappa_k -> 1, so unconditionally 'for every eps > 0 there is k(eps) with proportion >= 1 - eps of zeros of xi^{(k)} simple AND on the line' - de-conditionalizing the Farmer-Gonek program. HONEST LIMIT: this yields nothing for zeta itself: differentiation is smoothing, Rodgers-Tao Lambda >= 0 says there is no margin for any un-smoothing bootstrap, interlacing arguments require realness of the zeros being descended from, and Conrey (1983) already gives on-line proportion -> 1 for xi^{(k)} without RH content. The new content is per-k simplicity constants, k=1 optimality, and the family-of-derivatives ladder; it is a proportions machine for derivative zeros, not a zeta channel.

SUB-DIRECTION (iii) - HYBRID UNIFORMITY (designed, subordinate). For q <= T^theta the individual (no averaging) certificate runs with X = (qT)^Lambda <= T^{1-eps} (MV still the binding step), Lambda < 1/(1+theta): re-deriving Sections 5-6 with all constants uniform in (q,T) gives N0s_chi(T,2T] >= (H(1/(1+theta)) - o(1)) N_chi uniformly, positive for theta < sqrt(6)/3 = 0.8165 - the first unconditional positive-proportion critical-line theorem uniform in conductor up to q = T^{4/5}. Gluing (iii) to Tier 1 gives one two-regime uniform theorem covering all (q,T) with T >= (log q)^{1+delta}.

WHICH SUB-DIRECTION YIELDS A STATEMENT ABOUT ZETA ITSELF STRONGER THAN 2/3: within the two-moment certificate, none - there are no cross-L-function interaction terms, so no Deuring-Heilbronn-type repulsion can be expressed (an off-line zero of one L(s,chi) is a signature-(1,1) block in one summand of the direct sum; it cannot influence another summand). This is stated honestly. The genuine zeta-facing bridge is technological: Tier 2's averaged shifted-convolution/dispersion estimates are the SAME estimates whose t-aspect analogue ('averaged Hardy-Littlewood' partial evaluation of the O1 off-diagonal at effective lambda slightly > 1) is the paper's own named route past the 0.6818 ceiling for zeta (support 1.04 buys 0.70). The family program is the proving ground where that machinery gets built unconditionally in an easier (extra-average) setting first.

result.mechanism: COORDINATES AND OBJECTS. H_t(z) = int_0^infty e^{tu^2} Phi(u) cos(zu) du, H_0(z) = (1/8) xi(1/2 + iz/2); zeta zero rho = beta + i gamma corresponds to z = 2 gamma - 2i(beta - 1/2), so depth delta = beta - 1/2 becomes height y = 2 delta off the real z-axis. Forward flow (t increasing) obeys dH/dt = -H'': real zeros repel (Dyson-type, velocity 2 sum' 1/(x_j - x_k)), complex conjugate pairs attract the axis and a pair at height y dies (lands on the axis) at time ~ y^2/2; backward flow reverses both. Two monotone transport maps: real zeros stay real FORWARD; complex zeros stay complex BACKWARD. Local spacing at height x is ~ 4 pi / log(x/4pi), so the intrinsic relaxation scale of the flow at height T is t ~ 1/log^2 T. THE DIFFUSIVE SCALING: set L = log(T/2pi) and t = +/- 4 sigma / L^2 with sigma >= 0 fixed as T -> infinity. THE MULTIPLIER (the engine): the heat flow multiplies the mode of frequency u (z-side) by e^{t u^2}. In gamma-coordinates (z = 2 gamma) the Riemann-Siegel term n oscillates at local frequency omega_n = theta'(gamma) - log n, and the flow multiplier relative to the carrier (n=1, omega_1 = theta'(gamma) = (1/2)log(gamma/2pi) ~ L/2) is m_n = e^{(t/4)(omega_n^2 - omega_1^2)} = e^{(t/4) log n (log n - L)} = e^{-/+ sigma alpha (1 - alpha)}, alpha = log n / L in [0,1] (minus for forward t = +4 sigma/L^2). Hence H_t has an explicit-formula density nu^{(t)} = mu_t + P_X^{(t)} whose 'von Mangoldt' coefficients are Lambda_t(n) = Lambda(n) e^{-sigma alpha(1-alpha)} (1 + o(1)) — the flow is EXACTLY a Gaussian-in-log reweighting of the prime side, trivial at alpha = 0 (density) and alpha = 1 (band edge), maximal at alpha = 1/2. Consistency checks: (i) at sigma -> infinity backward this reproduces quantitatively the Rodgers-Tao mechanism for Lambda >= 0 (fixed forward flow time would force F(alpha) -> 0 on (0,1), contradicting the unconditional Fejer mass 1/3); (ii) forward damping = rigidification matches Dyson repulsion toward the local lattice; backward amplification (e^{+2 sigma alpha(1-alpha)}) = clustering matches attraction/collisions. THE CERTIFICATE FAMILY: run the entire Zeta23 pipeline on H_t. Zero side is instantiation-agnostic (ZeroConfig needs only reflection symmetry + local finiteness + log-density — H_t qualifies for every t); Lemma R, inertia, Poisson sampling, tail bound apply verbatim (the strip widens to |y| <= 1 + O(sigma/L^2): harmless in the X^{1/2}-tail). Mollified Gram Certificates: Euler-Product Weights inside the Weil-Form Inertia Method
result.thesis: Put the Levinson/Conrey mollifier inside the evaluation vectors of the Zeta23 Gram matrix — G^B_kl = W(b⋆f_k, b⋆f_l) with b a Möbius-derived Dirichlet-polynomial weight — so that the same formalized inertia/rank-trace certificate consumes twisted (multiplicative) moments instead of bare bandwidth-one L² data, producing an unconditional certificate family that provably cannot exist for Davenport-Heilbronn/Epstein (their log-derivative and inverse coefficients grow polynomially) and whose quantified target is to beat the Montgomery-Taylor optimum 0.6725 and the formalized 0.6818287 bandwidth-one ceiling.
result.mechanism:
OBJECT. For a real sequence b = (b_m), b_1 = 1, supp b ⊆ [1, M], M = (T/2π)^θ, define the multiplicative convolution (b⋆f)(u) = Σ_m (b_m/√m) f(u − log m), so that (b⋆f)^(τ) = B(1/2+iτ) f̂(τ) with B(s) = Σ_m b_m m^{−s}. The mollified Weil form is W_B(f,g) := W(b⋆f, b⋆g), and the mollified Gram matrix is G^B_kl = W_B(f_k, f_l) on the SAME critical-density Gabor family f_k = φ(u)e^{−iτ_k u} (τ_k = T + 2πk/L, d = ⌊LT/2π⌋, L = λ log(T/2π)) as the two-thirds paper. Spectral-density form: W_B(f,g) = ∫ f̂(τ) conj(ĝ(τ)) |B(1/2+iτ)|² ν_{X'}(τ) dτ with X' = e^L M² — the arithmetic weight sits in the density, the taper and grid are untouched.

ZERO SIDE (σ-equivariance — why the block machinery survives verbatim). Expanding as in Prop 4.1: c*G^B c = Σ_ρ m_ρ B(ρ)conj(B(1−ρ̄)) ℓ_{γρ}(c) conj(ℓ_{γ_{1−ρ̄}}(c)). An on-line zero ρ = 1/2+iγ contributes a rank-one PSD atom with EFFECTIVE MASS m_ρ β_ρ, β_ρ = |B(1/2+iγ)|² ≥ 0. An off-line pair {ρ, 1−ρ̄} contributes the 2×2 block [[0, w_ρ],[conj(w_ρ), 0]], w_ρ = m_ρ B(ρ)conj(B(1−ρ̄)) ∈ C, of signature (1,1) if w_ρ ≠ 0 and (0,0) if w_ρ = 0 — never more than one positive square. Because the weight attached to the pair is a single scalar respecting the ρ ↦ 1−ρ̄ symmetry, Lemma 3.1 (pull-back inertia, needing no independence) gives exactly as before: Ĝ^B = P_B + Q_B + E_B with P_B ⪰ 0, rank P_B ≤ s₁+s₂, n₊(Q_B) ≤ p, and tail ‖E_B‖ ≪ l³ T^{(λ+2θ)/2−1} (Prop 4.2 with X → XM²; the C³ taper suffices since |B(ρ)| ≤ M^{|β−1/2|}·Σ|b_m|/√m off the line). The Lean lemma rank_trace_mult_k (RankTraceMult.lean:369) is already stated for ARBITRARY real weights m_j ≥ 0 — the paper's own hook for exactly these non-integer effective multiplicities.

PRIME SIDE (where the Euler product enters). With normalization n(b) := Σ_m b_m²/m = 1, the two moments become mollified/twisted mean values, evaluable unconditionally for λ + 2θ ≤ 1 by the paper's own Montgomery-Vaughan step (Lemma 5.2 applies to arbitrary coefficients):
(1) tr Ĝ^B = (m₁(b,λ) + o(1))N, m₁ = 1 − 2𝒞(b)/λ·(explicit window factor), where 𝒞(b) = Σ_{n≥2} (Λ(n)/n) Σ_m b_{mn} b_m/m is the mollifier-prime correlation. Via Landau-Gonek this equals the weighted zero count Σ_ρ m_ρ B(ρ)conj(B(1−ρ̄))/N. For b = μ(m)ψ(log(M/m)/log M): b_{mp}b_m = −μ²(m)ψψ ≤ 0, giving m₁ = 1 + 2θ·Ã(ψ) + O(θ²), Ã(ψ) = ∫₀¹ (∫ψ(u)ψ(u+v)du/∫ψ²) dv > 0 — an ORDER-θ gain in the trace with no log T loss, the analytic shadow of Λ⋆μ = −μ·log (differentiated Euler product).
(2) ‖Ĝ^B‖²_F = L²∫∫Φ(τ−τ')² ν_B(τ)ν_B(τ')dτdτ' = (m₂(b,λ) + o(1))N, ν_B = |B|²ν. Main terms: (a) window-Plancherel ⟨|B|²⟩²-part ↦ (1/λ₁)·⟨|B|⁴⟩-corrected — here Möbius does real work: for the μ-mollifier ⟨|B|⁴⟩/⟨|B|²⟩² stays O(1) (mollifier fourth moments), whereas a generic coefficient sequence of that length is log-divergent; (b) the mollified prime diagonal (Λ·b-correlation)² ↦ deformed λ/3-term; (c) a NEW cross-diagonal μ̄·d(p)·Λ(p)-term (mollifier oscillation × prime oscillation at matched frequency log p) carrying the Fejér triangle weight — absent at b = δ₁, where the μP_X cross term integrates to zero by oscillation.

CERTIFICATES. Two branches, both weight-agnostic in the linear algebra:
(CS branch, first theorem) n₊(H) ≥ (tr H)₊²/‖H‖²_F for any Hermitian H (Lemma 3.3, in repo) + inertia + Riemann-von Mangoldt gives N₀^dist(T,2T) ≥ (2 m₁(b,λ)²/m₂(b,λ) − 1 − o(1)) N. Unmollified value: 2·(3/4)−1 = 1/2 at λ=1. The mollified ratio m₁²/m₂ is a new arithmetic quantity outside the κ(λ) = 1/λ + λ/3 curve.
(Lemma-R branch, second stage) rank_trace_mult_k with weights w_j = t·m_ρβ_ρ, scale t optimized: distinct-count ≥ (m₁²/m₂)N; recovering the SIMPLE-zero level requires per-atom saturation control k_c(tβ_ρ) — governed by the distribution of β_ρ over zeros (fourth mollified discrete moment), the designated second paper.

FIRST-VARIATION FORMULA (the decision instrument). Perturbing b = δ₁ + (mollifier direction) yields d/dθ [m₁²/m₂] = Σ_p (log p/p)·G(α_p)·(profile weights) + o(1), α_p = log p/log(T/2π), with G(α) an explicit elementary function assembled from: +4Ã-type trace gain (flat window weight) versus the cross-diagonal cost in m₂ (triangle weight (λ−α)); both terms trace to the SAME correlation 𝒞(b) integrated against different kernels, so G is a purely archimedean, computable function. Its sign profile on (0, θ] decides whether short Möbius weights (or, with opposite sign, short Euler-product resonators) improve the certificate — and the finite-T numerics measure it directly.

TWO REGIMES. Regime I (first theorem): λ + 2θ ≤ 1 — every mean value inside Montgomery-Vaughan; fully unconditional with the paper's error budget. Regime II (milestone 3): λ = 1 with θ > 0 — the off-diagonals become exactly the shifted-convolution sums of the TWISTED second moment ∫|ζ|²|B|⁴-type, i.e. Deshouillers-Iwaniec/Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown/Bettin-Chandee-Radziwiłł Kloosterman technology (twisted second moment known to mollifier length T^{17/33}) — proven multiplicative input STRICTLY beyond bandwidth-one pair-correlation data, entering exactly at the hook the paper names (Prop 5.6's off-diagonal).

DH/EPSTEIN SEPARATION (design principle, provable). For f with a zero at σ₀ > 1 (Davenport-Heilbronn; Epstein with h > 1), (i) the log-derivative coefficients Λ_f(n) are Ω(n^{σ₀−1−ε}) along a sequence (abscissa of −f'/f is ≥ σ₀), so the prime-side second-moment evaluation fails at every window — the paper already notes Prop 5.6 dies; and (ii) the inverse 1/f has coefficient partial sums Ω(x^{σ₀−ε}), so NO bounded-coefficient mollifier exists: 𝒞(b) and ⟨|B|⁴⟩ cannot be simultaneously controlled. Both facts are short abscissa-theory lemmas. The certificate family is provably EMPTY for these RH-false objects at the level of inputs, not outputs — the first positivity statement in this program whose engine, not merely whose conclusion, requires the Euler product.

GROWING-SUPPORT MARGIN PROGRAM (contact with Connes-Consani). On compact supports [1/X, X] the campaign measured margin(W) ≈ e^{−4πX} (prolate spheroidal eigenvalue leakage, mechanism located in CC 2006.13771/2106.01715). The mollified prediction: margin(W_B) with B = truncated Euler product of 1/ζ (primes ≤ X) decays with a strictly smaller rate constant, because the |B|²-weight suppresses the prime-side pressure that pins the margin to the prolate floor — the semilocal transition (Euler factors entering one at a time, CCM 2310.18423) made quantitative. First instance: re-run the certified [1/3,3] computation (primes 2,3,5,7) with baby weights B = truncations of (1−2^{−s}), (1−2^{−s})(1−3^{−s}); measure the slope. A proven margin law e^{−cX}, c < 4π, for the mollified form on growing supports would be a new quantitative form of 'the Euler product buys positivity'.

The Zeta23 paper (2026) explores only the scalar taper and unweighted higher moments (§7.5 d-f) and explicitly lists 'mollifiers/Levinson-Conrey machinery, amplification' as outside its formalized ceiling's scope without constructing anything there. (2) Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek 1998 / Bui-Heath-Brown 2013 compute mollified discrete moments over zeros and reach 19/27 simple — but ONLY under RH (zeros on the line are needed for their Cauchy-Schwarz over zeros and their Gonek-lemma evaluations); this proposal is precisely 'CGG made unconditional' by the same inertia move with which the paper made Montgomery unconditional — the natural but unclaimed next rung. (3) BGSTB 2306.04799 and Goldston-Suriajaya remove RH from pair correlation but stay strictly in unweighted L² data (bandwidth-one); the mollified moments m₁, m₂ are twisted data outside that class. (6) The DH-separation theorem — a certificate family provably empty for explicit RH-false objects because its INPUTS need bounded-coefficient invertibility — has no antecedent; it converts the campaign's barrier-checker philosophy into a theorem. [Flagged for verification: possible 2025-26 literature on 'weighted pair correlation' with |ζ'(ρ)|-type weights — all known instances are RH-conditional and produce no unconditional on-line counts.]

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Campaign residue: 'every route's first substantive step was Weil positivity in disguise'; G1-G4 per-pair pricing false; Pontryagin route empty; Radziwill mollifier limitations
evades_obstructions.how: First substantive step here is an EVALUATION (mollified moment asymptotics — unconditional theorems of Levinson-standard difficulty), not a positivity assumption; the only positivity is the same finite-dimensional inertia that already produced Theorems A-E. New leverage beyond the paper: twisted arithmetic data (Lambda*mu = -mu*log cancellation, bounded Moebius fourth moments, Landau-Gonek zero-prime correlations) provably invisible to bandwidth-one L2 data. Pricing stays mass-linear (weights multiply masses inside rank_trace_mult_k; no per-pair quadratic integrality). Positive index/rank counting only — no negative-index counting. Radziwill's intrinsic mollifier-length ceilings for LEVINSON's functional do not transfer to the Gram-moment functional, but are cited as calibration: theta-limits will bind and milestone 2 quantifies the exchange rate rather than assuming it is favorable.

milestones: M1 (first theorem, ~6-12 months): the Regime-I mollified certificate — structure, unconditional moments m1/m2, distinct-zero certificate 2m1^2/m2 - 1, and the explicit first-variation function G(alpha); numerics-validated at finite T.

M2: joint variational problem over (window phi, profile psi) at fixed total bandwidth lambda + 2theta <= 1 — the mollified analogue of Theorem D's Euler-Lagrange problem; outcome either an improved constant at bandwidth <= 1 or a clean 'mollification-vs-bandwidth exchange' no-go theorem, both formalizable with the ThmD/PairCeiling templates.

M3: Regime II — lambda = 1 with theta > 0 by twisted-second-moment technology (Deshouillers-Iwaniec / Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill shifted-convolution estimates adapted to the Phi-smoothed bilinear form); explicit target V(1,theta*) > 0.6725 (first improvement past the Montgomery-Taylor optimum), stretch target > 0.68183 (first certificate strictly beyond the formalized bandwidth-one ceiling, using proven multiplicative input).

M4: separation theorems — abscissa lemmas showing the certificate family is empty for Davenport-Heilbronn and class-number>1 Epstein at the level of inputs; Lean formalization of the weighted block layer + separation (first formalized multiplicativity-sensitive yes-go/no-go pair).

M5: simple-zeros version via rank_trace_mult_k saturation control (distribution of beta_rho over zeros; fourth mollified discrete moment), and the growing-support margin program: mollified re-run of the certified [1/3,3] positivity with Euler-factor weights, then rigorous margin lower bounds e^{-cX}, c < 4pi, with M(X) coupled to support — quantitative contact with the Connes-Consani semilocal program.

M6 (horizon): the moment ladder V(1,theta) as twisted-moment theorems improve; extend the 256-law exact-rational LP with twisted-moment rows to compute the enlarged class's own ceiling — the program's falsifiable wall.

result.numerics: Two runnable experiments (Python/mpmath + numpy, hours-scale; or Wolfram). EXPERIMENT A (certificate gain curve): take the first 10^4 zeros (gamma <= 9878, mpmath.zetazero or Odlyzko tables) and the window gamma in [5000, 9878]; lambda = 1, L = log(T/2pi) ~ 6.7, d ~ 7000; build the zero-side weighted matrix directly from zeros with beta_rho = |B(1/2 + i*gamma)|^2 for b = delta_1 and b = mu(m)*psi smoothed, M in {20, 100, 500, 2000}, psi in {1, linear, quadratic}; compute R1 = sum beta_rho/(N*n(b)), R2 = Frobenius/N, and both certificates (2R1^2/R2 - 1 and 4R1 - R2 - 2). Simultaneously compute the PRIME-side predictions m1, m2 from the derived formulas (primes <= X*M^2) and check closure of the explicit-formula bookkeeping to 2-3 digits — this validates the moment identities before any proof. Signal: the finite-T certificates are known to sit near +0.40-0.42 (paper section 8), so measure the DIFFERENCE mollified-minus-unmollified as a function of theta = log M/log(T/2pi) and compare with the first-variation prediction sum_p (log p/p) G(alpha_p): sign and slope of the empirical gain curve directly test whether G > 0 — the route's go/no-go datum. EXPERIMENT B (margin law): reimplement the campaign's positivity-margin curve (ball/interval arithmetic, supports [1/X, X], X in [1, 3], primes 2,3,5,7 — the tx_005-015 setup) for W_B with baby Euler weights B = truncations of (1-2^{-s}), (1-2^{-s})(1-3^{-s}), (1-2^{-s})^{-1}: fit log-margin vs X and compare the slope against the empirical 4pi of the unweighted form. A measurably smaller slope for the 1/zeta-direction weights is direct evidence that the Euler product buys positivity margin (the M5 conjecture); no change, or a larger slope, is evidence against and would redirect M5 to the resonator sign."
result.payoff: M1 lands: a new unconditional certificate family with explicit value 2m1^2/m2 - 1 generalizing the paper's 1/2-distinct branch, the first-variation function G(alpha) in closed form, and validated explicit-formula bookkeeping — the machinery paper. M2 lands: either a constant strictly above H(lambda_tot) at total bandwidth <= 1 (first demonstration that arithmetic weights beat raw bandwidth) or a new formalizable no-go quantifying the mollifier-bandwidth exchange rate — either outcome extends the formalized no-go library and the LP-ceiling template. M3 lands: V(1,theta) > 0.6725 breaks the Montgomery-Taylor optimum (proven ceiling of ALL windows on unweighted data) with proven multiplicative input; V > 0.68183 breaks the formalized bandwidth-one ceiling itself — the headline result, and the first concrete instance of the paper's own price-list hook ('any partial information beyond alpha = 1 plugs into Prop 5.6'). M4 lands: the DH-filter becomes a theorem pair (nonempty for zeta, empty for DH/Epstein), the first formalized multiplicativity-sensitive separation — a reusable refutation channel for future proposals. M5 lands: unconditional simple-zero improvements past 2/3, and a proven mollified margin law e^{-cX}, c < 4pi, giving the Connes-Consani semilocal program its first quantitative arithmetic target. M6: each new twisted-moment theorem converts to a constant on a published ladder, with the enlarged class's ceiling computed by the same exact-rational LP — the program polices itself.
failure_modes: The first-variation function G(alpha) could be <= 0 throughout (the cross-diagonal cost in m2 dominating the trace gain 4*theta*A-tilde): mollification would then never help at any bandwidth — the route degrades to the M2 no-go theorem (publishable, formalizable, but no constant improvement).

The fluctuation of beta_rho = |B(rho)|^2 over zeros (log-normal-type) could inflate the zero-side diagonal of m2 enough to eat the trace gain even when G > 0 in the mean — visible early in Experiment A.
Landau-Gonek uniformity in mollifier length M <= T^theta may carry worse error terms than assumed (flagged); would shrink the admissible theta range in M1 but not kill it.

Regime II adaptation of Deshouillers-Iwaniec/BCR shifted-convolution estimates to the Phi-smoothed Gabor bilinear form (rather than |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 weights) may lose the needed uniformity — M3 could stall at lambda < 1 + theta compensation below the 0.6725 target.

Finite-T numerics may be too far from the asymptotic regime (paper section 8's warning) for the gain curve to be resolvable above noise at 10^4 zeros; mitigation: measure differences at matched windows, push to 10^5 zeros via Odlyzko tables.

Possible overlap with unexamined 2025-26 'weighted pair correlation' or mollified-discrete-moment preprints (e.g. successors of 2508.11108 or Goldston-Suriajaya) — a literature pass is required before claiming the framing 'CGG made unconditional' (flagged).

The simple-zeros extension (M5) needs per-atom saturation control k_c(t*beta_rho) governed by fourth mollified discrete moments — potentially out of reach unconditionally, capping the program at distinct-zero improvements.

result.title: The Wanted Poster: a depth-uniform, every-window localization of the two-thirds certificate, as the core of an honest RH-refutation program
result.thesis: Because the Zeta23 inertia certificate is completely blind to the depth |β−1/2| of off-line zeros, re-running it in windows of length H = T^θ (θ > 3−√6 ≈ 0.5505) around an arbitrary height yields the first structural constraints that hold uniformly down to depth 10^(−1000) — a certified "wanted poster" saying any RH counterexample must be shallow, locally sparse at every polynomial scale, and immersed in a ≥(2−1/θ−θ/3)-fraction simple-on-line environment — which simultaneously kills the dense-carrier-wave failure scenario, organizes the Λ>0 and statistics channels honestly, and identifies the cheapest new statistic (band-edge regularity of the unconditional form factor at α=1) that would shrink both the formal ceiling and the Alternative-Hypothesis world.
result.mechanism:
OBJECTS. Fix θ ∈ (3−√6, 1], a window I = (T, T+H] with H = T^θ, and bandwidth λ = θ−ε′ < θ, L = λ·log(T/2π), X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ. Take the paper's Gabor family f_k(u) = φ(u)e^{−iτ_k u} on the grid τ_k = T + 2πk/L, but now with d = ⌊HL/2π⌋ ≈ λ·N(I) frequencies covering only I (the Gabor–Poisson identity Σ_k φ̂(γ−τ_k)φ̂(γ′−τ_k) = LΦ(γ−γ′) is grid-translation-invariant — Poisson.lean proves it for arbitrary offset T — so nothing in the zero side cares where the window sits). Form G_kl = W(f_k,f_l) from the Weil explicit formula.

ZERO SIDE (already window-parametric in the repo): Â = P + Q + tail exactly as in Prop 4.1/ZeroBlockData: P ⪰ 0 from on-line points in I′ = (T−D₀, T+H+D₀], rank P ≤ s₁+s₂, tr P ≤ N_on(I′) via the sampling identity; each off-line pair {ρ, 1−ρ̄} with ordinate in I′ a signature-(1,1) block with n₊(Q) ≤ p_I, REGARDLESS of depth — this is the depth-blindness that classical zero-density methods lack. Rank–trace at c = 2 (Lemma R, formalized, provably tight): 3s₁ + 4s₂ + 4p_I ≥ 4·tr Â − ‖Â‖²_F.

PRIME SIDE, localized (the only genuinely new work): tr G̃ over the short grid = aL·N(I)(1+o(1)) — the μ-density integral localizes trivially (μ ≈ l/2π is flat across I), and the P_X contribution is O(L√X) = O(l·T^{λ/2}) = o(Hl) since λ < 2θ. For the second moment, the diagonal prime term gives (H/π)·Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)²n^{−1}g(log n) ≈ HL³/6π, while the off-diagonal is bounded by the SAME window-independent Montgomery–Vaughan estimate O₁ ≪ L²X as in Prop 5.6 (MV with δ_n = 1/(2n) bounds the bilinear form by the diagonal Σ Λ(n)²·n·n^{−1} ≈ XL with no window factor; this is visible in the Lean file PPOffDiag.lean:40, whose bound 16·C_MV·(∫Φ²)·Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)² contains no T). Admissibility: L²X = o(HL³) ⟺ X = o(HL) ⟺ λ < θ. Tail: choose the free parameter D₀ = T^{θ/4+ε} (Prop 4.2 allows any D₀ ∈ [T^{λ/4+ε}, T^{1−ε}]), giving θ₀ ≪ l·T^{λ/2−θ/2−2ε} → 0 and boundary count N(I′∖I) ≪ D₀·l = o(Hl). Hence, unconditionally, tr Ĝ = N(I)(1+o(1)) and ‖Ĝ‖²_F = (κ(λ)+o(1))·N(I), κ(λ) = 1/λ + λ/3.

OUTPUT (the wanted poster). Combining as in §6, for every window I of length H = T^θ:
(a) N₀ˢ(I) ≥ (2 − 1/θ − θ/3 − ε)·N(I) — simple-and-on-line zeros in EVERY short window;
(b) N_off(I) ≤ (1/θ + θ/3 − 1 + ε)·N(I) — from N(I) ≥ N_on(I) ≥ s₁ and (a): off-line zeros (with multiplicity) cannot exceed local density κ(θ)−1; numerically ≤ 0.334·N(I) at θ=1, ≤ 0.412 at θ=0.9, ≤ 0.517 at θ=0.8, ≤ 0.662 at θ=0.7, ≤ 0.867 at θ=0.6, vacuous at θ ≤ 3−√6;
(c) N_d(I) ≥ ((3−1/θ−θ/3)/2 − ε)·N(I). With the Montgomery–Taylor window (ThmD machinery at bandwidth θ), 1/θ+θ/3 improves to 1/c*_θ.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT REFUTATION INSTRUMENT. (1) Depth-uniformity: every classical constraint on off-line zeros (Guth–Maynard N(σ,T) ≪ T^{30(1−σ)/13}, all zero-density technology) degenerates as δ = β−1/2 → 0 and says literally nothing for δ ≪ 1/log T — exactly the Lehmer/carrier-wave regime where a counterexample would live (Farmer 2211.11671). Inertia prices a pair at depth 10^(−1000) identically to depth 0.4. (2) Every-window (not almost-all): the constraint holds at the counterexample's own height γ₀, so it directly constrains the neighborhood of any hypothetical off-line zero: at all scales γ₀^θ, θ > 0.5505, its companions are outnumbered ≥ 2:1 by certified simple on-line zeros (θ=1). (3) It kills the dense-failure scenario: Farmer's carrier-wave picture, in its off-line variant, has long stretches of zeros pushed off the line by a slow modulation; (b) forbids off-line local density 1 in any window longer than γ₀^{0.5505+ε}, and density > 1/3 at scale γ₀. (4) It closes the loop with Part I's visibility analysis: the transcript's empirical visibility thresholds required an isolation hypothesis (HR); the wanted poster CERTIFIES partial isolation (sparsity at all polynomial scales) unconditionally, making a visibility theorem under certified sparsity (milestone 6) meaningful for the first time.

CHANNEL ASSESSMENTS BUILT INTO THE PROGRAM. Λ-channel: since Rodgers–Tao gives Λ ≥ 0, a certified Λ ≥ 10^{−N} is logically equivalent to ¬RH; concretely it requires a certified non-real zero of some H_t, t > 0 (a finite argument-principle/interval-arithmetic computation, Polymath15's effective machinery reused in reverse — feasible IF one knows where to look), and no independent shortcut exists: backward heat flow from Λ ≤ 0.2 data is exponentially ill-posed, and forward flow of an RH-true configuration keeps all zeros real for every t > 0. So the honest role of the Λ-channel is the quantitative bridge: an off-line zero of depth δ at height γ₀ forces Λ ≳ c·δ²/polylog(γ₀) via the pair-attraction ODE dy/dt ≈ −1/y of the flow (exact exponent to be pinned in milestone 6; the qualitative statement Λ > 0 ⟺ such a zero exists is Rodgers–Tao + de Bruijn) — converting any future find into a certified strictly-positive Λ. Statistics channel: Farmer is right for zero-statistics — any functional of zeros below height T is trivially consistent with both worlds; the formalizable small no-go (milestone 5) exhibits two ZeroConfigs in the repo's abstract configuration language agreeing below T, satisfying all certified constraints, one RH-true and one not; the only genuine influence channel is prime sums of length e^{c/δ} (to resolve depth δ), computationally void for δ ≪ 1. AH assessment: the Alternative Hypothesis fully survives the new theorems — the 256-periodic ceiling law (marks {1,2}, near-CUE band data, simple fraction 0.68183 > 2/3) is itself an AH-flavored world consistent with every theorem in the artifact, including the localized ones (which consume only bandwidth-one data). AH forces the form factor to be 2-periodic, so F_AH(1+u) = 1−u+o(1) versus F_GUE = 1 on (1,2); the discriminators are (i) the band-edge derivative/regularity of F at α = 1⁺ and (ii) the Wiener long-run average of F, which under AH equals the sum of squared atoms of the half-integer spacing measure — to be tested against the RH-conditional Carneiro–Milinovich–Ramos window [0.9303, 1.3208] (whether GLSS Part II arXiv:2507.06823 already computes this average must be checked — flagged). The cheapest constraint provable with current technology is edge regularity of the unconditional BGSTB complex-zero form factor AT α = 1 (no atom at the band edge): it is exactly the free row j = N that the 256-law exploits (edge atom of mass 0.826, D(1) = 0.824), it is listed in the repo as an extension hook, and it requires only mollified/second-moment information at Dirichlet-polynomial length exactly T — not length T^{1+ε}.
result.novelty: Relative to the Zeta23 paper: all its theorems are dyadic-window (T,2T] statements; localization in window position/length is an axis the 54-hour campaign never varied (it varied bandwidth, moments, weights, and windows-as-tapers only). Relative to short-interval literature: Karatsuba (1984, H ≥ T^{27/82}) and successors give ≫ H log T critical-line zeros in short intervals but no explicit proportion near 2/3, no simplicity, and — decisively — no upper bound on off-line counts; to my knowledge NO short-interval simple-zero proportion exists at any exponent (flagged for a literature check), and no off-line local-density cap of any kind exists that is uniform in depth. Relative to zero-density (Guth–Maynard arXiv:2405.20552 and the ANTEDB successors): those bounds are vacuous for depth δ ≪ 1/log T; (b) is the first constraint of positive strength in that regime. Relative to GLSS arXiv:2503.15449/2507.06823: their 100%-simple conclusions assume full-support PCC; ours are unconditional and local. Relative to Farmer arXiv:2211.11671: converts "no reasons to doubt" from a rebuttal-essay into certified structural theorems a counterexample must satisfy, and makes his no-statistic claim a formal no-go within a precise certificate class while exhibiting the exact loophole (prime sums of length e^{c/δ}). Relative to Rodgers–Tao: adds the explicit depth→Λ quantitative bridge as a stated target rather than folklore. The refutation-program framing itself — wanted poster (structure) + bridge (Λ) + no-go (statistics) as one certified search-space-narrowing instrument — has no antecedent; the literature has "no serious counterexample-search program exists" (literature.md §9).

evades_obstructions.obstruction: DH/Epstein filter
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope, and honestly so: the program claims structure/refutation constraints, never full RH. Additionally the localized certificate is not even available for DH/Epstein: their log-derivative coefficients are uncontrolled (DH has zeros with β > 1, so −F′/F coefficients grow polynomially; Epstein class# > 1 similarly), so the prime-side mean-value step (Prop 5.6) fails for them — the certificate consumes an input those objects violate, which is why they may (and do) have off-line zeros our theorem would forbid for ζ.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Alternative Hypothesis (bandwidth-1 indistinguishability)
evades_obstructions.how: Confronted head-on rather than evaded: the program's own assessment is that AH survives the 2/3 theorem (the 256-law is an AH-flavored certified witness). The localized first theorem uses only bandwidth-one data and therefore cannot and does not claim to kill AH. Milestone 4 designs the cheapest AH-killers: band-edge regularity of F at α=1 (within length-T technology) and the Wiener average of F against the CMR interval (RH-conditional).

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bandwidth-one certificate ceiling 0.6818287
evades_obstructions.how: No claimed constant exceeds it: the localized constants 2−1/θ−θ/3 ≤ 2−1/c*_1 = 0.6725 < 0.68183. Localization in window position is orthogonal to form-factor bandwidth, so the ceiling does not obstruct it. The only ceiling-attacking milestone (M4) goes through an added edge constraint at α=1, which the formalized ceiling explicitly does NOT cover (the law's row j=N is free; constraining it is a listed extension hook in the repo).

evades_obstructions.obstruction: lemmaR_tight (two-moment certificate exhausted)
evades_obstructions.how: The linear algebra is reused verbatim, not improved; tightness caps the constants H(θ), not the ability to run the certificate in new windows. No claim of separating on-line doubles from deep pairs is made anywhere.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Dimension cap d = λN
evades_obstructions.how: Respected per window: d ≈ λN(I) with λ < θ, and the theorem is only claimed for θ > 3−√6 > 1/2 where the certificate is non-vacuous; the vacuity below θ = 0.5505 is stated as the theorem's own boundary.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: κ(λ) = 1/λ+λ/3 ≥ 2/√3 (0.8453 cap at any bandwidth)
evades_obstructions.how: No proportion above 0.8453 is claimed at any point of the program; the wanted-poster constants are all ≤ 0.6725.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bombieri small-support Weil positivity (unconditional cones prove nothing)
evades_obstructions.how: The mechanism is not a positivity proof on a cone: it is a two-sided counting certificate (inertia + rank–trace) whose output includes UPPER bounds on off-line counts — a direction small-support positivity cannot produce. To the campaign residue 'every route's first substantive step was Weil positivity in disguise': our first step is the already-proven rank–trace certificate; the NEW leverage is localization in window position/length plus the refutation reading (upper-bounding N_off), neither of which is a positivity statement.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bombieri–Garrett ~94% pseudo-Laplacian cap
evades_obstructions.how: No pseudo-Laplacian or automorphic-spectrum route is used; out of scope.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Parity problem
evades_obstructions.how: No sieve-only step anywhere; the arithmetic inputs are EF + Chebyshev + Montgomery–Vaughan mean values, all already formalized.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Conrey–Li (de Branges positivity fails)
evades_obstructions.how: No de Branges positivity condition is assumed; the de Branges δ-tilt appears only as unmined residue and is not on the critical path.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0
evades_obstructions.how: Absorbed as the organizing fact of the Λ-channel: since Λ ≥ 0, certifying Λ ≥ 10^{−N} is equivalent to certifying ¬RH via a complex zero of some H_t, t>0; the program therefore does NOT propose a standalone Λ-computation (backward flow is exponentially ill-posed — stated as a no-go) and instead supplies the depth→Λ bridge as a payoff formula for any future find.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Per-pair quadratic integrality pricing is FALSE (G1–G4)
evades_obstructions.how: Only the mass-linear rank–trace inequality is used; no per-pair quadratic pricing appears.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Pontryagin negative-index route empty
evades_obstructions.how: Not used; the positive-index dual (the paper's own mechanism) is used throughout.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Radziwill mollifier limitations / Conrey–Li / Levinson ceilings
evades_obstructions.how: No mollifier-length-dependent step is used; mean values enter only through MV at length ≤ T^θ.

milestones: M1 (the first theorem, ~6 months): localized certificate in every window H = T^θ, θ > 3−√6, with constants H(θ) = 2−1/θ−θ/3 (flat) and 2−1/c*_θ (optimal window); paper + Lean skeleton (the abstract implication BlockInputs + short-window moments ⟹ (a),(b),(c) is provable in the repo today; the analytic short-window Facts are the long pole).

M4: a strictly lower formal ceiling (killing the 256-law), the first unconditional form-factor information at the band edge, and quantified pressure on AH — plus the LP-re-run methodology prices any future edge theorem before anyone proves it. M5: Farmer's dictum becomes a theorem with an exact loophole statement — ends speculative 'statistical evidence for/against RH' arguments within the covered class. Literature preemption partially undiscovered: a short-interval simplicity or off-line-cap result may exist (Karatsuba-school, Ivić, or recent BGSTB follow-ups such as arXiv:2603.28104 'zeros in a narrow vertical box'); must be checked before claiming (a)-novelty — though the depth-uniform off-line cap (b) has no plausible antecedent since inertia-based counting is new to the 2026 paper.

Scope honesty: the wanted poster constrains OFF-LINE failure scenarios only; a 'carrier-wave' near-failure that keeps all zeros on the line with pathological spacings is untouched by (b), and AH survives — the program says so explicitly, but a reader wanting counterexample-EXCLUSION will find only density constraints, never exclusion (the method is insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros, per the paper's own §1.5).

M4 may be hard: edge regularity of F at α=1 could secretly require length-T^{1+ε} information (the atom at the edge may be exactly as inaccessible as F beyond the band); the LP-re-run then only prices an unprovable theorem.

Numerics risk: at T = 5·10^4 the certificate is strictly negative (Remark 5.9 — convergence 1−O(1/log T)), so Experiment 1 measures trends and depth-uniformity, not asymptotic constants; over-reading it would be wishful — the deliverable is the frontier's SHAPE, with the honest caveat that finite-T exclusion thresholds are far from κ(θ)−1.

Mitigation: odd-power near-blindness of hyperbolic blocks is checked and quantified by Monte Carlo (numerics (b)) before proving; the LP can be re-run with the measured interaction penalty as an extra row.

Fallback constants remain new but smaller.

Endpoint degradation: lambda_a -> 1 losses (loglog/log) could swallow a small certified gain if p0^(3) - 0.6725 turns out to be only ~0.01.

result.first_theorem: THEOREM T1 (unconditional mixed triple trace at total bandwidth < 2). Let l = log(T/2pi), and let lambda_a, lambda_b, lambda_c in (0,1] satisfy sigma := lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c < 2. Let phi_w (w = a,b,c) be C^3 tapers supported in [-lambda_w l/2, lambda_w l/2] (the paper's TaperProfile class), and put G^{(w)}_{kl} = W(phi_w e^{-i tau_k u}, phi_w e^{-i tau_l u}) on the common grid tau_k = T + 2pi k/l, k < d = floor(lT/2pi). Then, with NO hypothesis, tr(G^{(a)} G^{(b)} G^{(c)}) = M3(phi_a,phi_b,phi_c) * (T/2pi) * l^3 * (1+o(1)), where M3 is the explicit pairing functional (mu^3 smooth term, three Lambda(n)^2-diagonal cross terms with kernels (phi_w^2 * phi_{w'}^2)-hat, and an O(1/l) same-prime-power triple diagonal sum_p (log p)^3 sum_{alpha,beta} p^{-alpha-beta}). Equivalently, for the true zeta multiset with complex ordinates gamma_rho = (rho-1/2)/i: sum over triples of zeros in (T,2T] of m1 m2 m3 Phi_a(g1-g2) Phi_b(g2-g3) Phi_c(g3-g1) equals its pairing/diagonal value + o(N l^3-normalized) — i.e. the CONNECTED triple form factor of zeta zeros is o(1) on the closed simplex of total Fourier support sigma < 2. // STATUS OF INPUTS: the explicit formula for C_c^2 tests, the Gabor-Poisson identity (window- and grid-generic), the tail bound, Chebyshev-Mertens, and the MV weighted Hilbert inequality are all proved and FORMALIZED in Zeta23 (WeilEF/, Poisson.lean, Tail/, MV/ including the unexploited spacing_four and two_point lemmas). The paper itself asserts (Section 7.5(e)) the equal-window case tr G^k in the Rudnick-Sarnak range k*lambda < 2 by 'the diagonal method' but neither proves it with errors nor uses it; Hejhal 1994 / Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 prove the triple/n-level asymptotics under RH (flag: their unconditional complex-ordinate remarks need verification against the originals). T1 is the BGSTB24 move — de-conditionalize by working with complex ordinates and MV — executed one correlation order up, with mixed windows. // ATTACK SKETCH: (1) Fubini + tail absorption reduces tr(G_aG_bG_c) to the triple integral of nu_X against L^3 Phi_a Phi_b Phi_c (each factor's Poisson identity is exact at sub-critical sampling). (2) Expand nu^3 into 27 pieces; every piece with <= 2 prime factors is Prop 5.5-5.7 technology verbatim (integration by parts against the cosine; bilinear MV). (3) The new piece P_a P_b P_c: exact relations n1 n2 = n3 give a convergent same-prime-power sum (subleading); near-relations are bounded by COMPOSITE-FREQUENCY MV: frequencies y = log(n1 n2) with coefficients (Lambda*Lambda)(m) m^{-1/2}, m <= Y = X_a X_b, spacing delta_m >= 1/(2m), against z = log n3, n3 <= X_c; MV gives << (sum_{m<=Y}(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2)^{1/2} (sum_{n<=X_c} Lambda(n)^2)^{1/2} << (Y l^3)^{1/2}(X_c l)^{1/2} = l^2 T^{sigma/2}, which is o(T l^3) precisely when sigma < 2 — the Rudnick-Sarnak boundary re-derived from the already-formalized MV lemma. Ratio-type frequencies log(n1/n2) have Farey spacing >= 1/(2 n1 n2) and are handled identically; sum_{m<=Y}(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2 ~ c Y l^3 is an unconditional Mertens-type computation. Referee-evaluable, unconditional, and strictly stronger than anything in print at correlation order 3.

result.mechanism: OBJECTS. Fix the common critical-density Gabor grid tau_k = T + 2pi k/l, l = log(T/2pi), d = floor(lT/2pi) = N(T,2T)(1+o(1)). For three C^3 tapers phi_a, phi_b, phi_c with supports lambda_w * l, lambda_w <= 1, form the three Gram matrices G^{(w)}_{kl} = W(phi_w e^{-i tau_k u}, phi_w e^{-i tau_l u}) on the SAME grid (sub-critical sampling keeps the Poisson identity exact per window: sum_k phihat_w(g - tau_k) phihat_w(g' - tau_k) = l * Phi_w(g - g'), Phi_w = (phi_w^2)^hat). The new functional is the mixed third moment tr(G_a G_b G_c). Zero side, by three Poisson resummations: tr(G_a G_b G_c) = l^3 * sum_{rho1,rho2,rho3} m1 m2 m3 Phi_a(g1-g2) Phi_b(g2-g3) Phi_c(g3-g1) + tail — a TRIPLE-correlation functional whose kernel has Fourier support in the simplex {xi1+xi2+xi3 = 0, |xi_w| <= lambda_w} of total width sigma = lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c. Because the windows may be UNEQUAL, sigma < 2 allows one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1 (e.g. (0.98, 0.5, 0.5)) — a corner the paper's equal-window analysis (3*lambda < 2 forces lambda < 2/3) never touched. // THE NEW INVARIANT. For CUE, Diaconis-Shahshahani exactness gives E[Tr U^{j1} Tr U^{j2} Tr U^{-(j1+j2)}] = 0 whenever j1 + j2 <= N_matrix: the CONNECTED 3-level form factor vanishes identically on the closed simplex sum|xi_i| <= 2 (repulsion exactly cancels all diagonal terms). T1 proves the zeta analogue unconditionally for sigma < 2: the triple sum equals its explicit pairing/diagonal value (computable from mu and Lambda^2-diagonals, NO Hardy-Littlewood input) + o(main). This 'connected-triple vanishing' is a constraint on the zero configuration that is (i) a theorem-target with proven-technology inputs, (ii) multilinear of degree 3, hence OUTSIDE the pair form factor, and (iii) generically violated by adversarial marked laws such as the 256-periodic law, which was optimized only against pair rows. // WHY UNCONDITIONAL (prime side). Expanding each G by the explicit-formula density nu_X = mu + Pi_X + P_X gives 27 pieces; all with <= 2 prime factors are the paper's Prop 5.5-5.7 machinery. The genuinely new piece P_a P_b P_c contains exact relations n1 n2 = n3 (same-prime-power sums, O(1)) and near-relations, bounded by composite-frequency Montgomery-Vaughan (coefficients (Lambda*Lambda)(m)/sqrt(m), m <= X_a X_b, spacing >= 1/2m): << l^2 T^{sigma/2} = o(T l^3) iff sigma < 2. The Rudnick-Sarnak boundary thus falls out of the SAME MV lemma already formalized in Zeta23/MV/. No pair-correlation support beyond [-1,1], no shifted-convolution Lambda-correlations, no fourth moment are needed anywhere. // THE CERTIFICATE (Lemma C target). Validity polynomial psi(m) = c1 m + c2 m^2 + c3 m^3 + c4 1_{m=1} with psi(m) <= 1 for all m >= 1 (forcing c3 <= 0, so the route OBEYS the odd-moment LP-dual no-go instead of fighting it: mass escaping to large eigenvalues only hurts the adversary). Zero side: A = P + Q as in Prop 4.1. tr A^3 = tr P^3 + 3 tr(P^2 Q) + 3 tr(P Q^2) + tr Q^3. Structural asset: an isolated hyperbolic pair block has eigenvalues ~ +/- mu, so its ODD traces nearly cancel — the X^{3y} depth explosion that makes the zero-side second moment unreadable termwise is absent at leading order in odd traces; Q enters the cubic row only through interactions and through its trace-asymmetry, both priced against epsilon * tr A^2 (globally prime-bounded) and n_+(Q) <= p by von Neumann-type bounds. On-line atoms are handled by the already-formalized Schur-Jensen + spectrum-transfer pair (valid for arbitrary g with g(0)=0), giving tr g(P) vs sum_j g(m_j ||v_j||^2) comparisons for cubic g. Section 7.5(g) — Schur-Horn majorization for f(x) = -x^2/9 + x^3/18 with window cos(8s/5), yielding N_d >= 0.85082 under RH — is the proof-of-concept that cubic accounting survives interactions WHEN the third trace exists; Lemma C is its unconditional extension with Q nonempty and mixed kernels, the single genuinely new piece of linear algebra. // PRICING BEFORE PROVING (the LP). Extend the 256-law exact-rational LP: columns = marked periodic configurations c (weights w_c >= 0, positions, marks in {1,2,3}); pair rows as before (near-CUE + free edge); NEW triple rows: the observables A3^c(j1,j2) = Re[F_c(j1) F_c(j2) conj(F_c(j1+j2))]/N (and Im), F_c(j) = sum_i m_i e^{2pi i j x_i/N}, constrained to their T1 values (= 0 in the open simplex j1 + j2 <= N, edges free) within tolerance tau3. Each row is LINEAR in w_c, so this remains an exact LP; its value p0^(3)(N) is the exact ceiling of the enlarged certificate class, and its DUAL solution is the candidate optimal (c0, r, rho3) certificate whose validity Lemma C must prove. The route thus computes the exact worth of the triple-correlation upgrade BEFORE the analytic work — and as a free by-product, the pair-only dual at the same N is the explicit candidate certificate closing the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap inside the old class.

(5) Adjacent novelty: the M1 LP doubles as the first test of the Alternative Hypothesis against 3-level restricted data, going beyond the pair-only AH analysis of arXiv:2507.06823. Flagged for verification: the exact unconditional status/remarks in Hejhal 1994 and Rudnick-Sarnak 1996, and the precise Diaconis-Shahshahani exactness range.
result.numerics: Two experiments, both Python (scipy.optimize.linprog / exact rationals via fractions + a column-generation loop) or Wolfram scale, runnable now. (A) TRIPLE-ROW CEILING LP. Configurations: c = (rational positions x_i in [0,N), marks m_i in {1,2,3}, sum m_i = N), N = 64 then 128. Observables per configuration: F_c(j) = sum_i m_i exp(2pi i j x_i / N); pair rows S_c(j) = |F_c(j)|^2 / N; triple rows A3_c(j1,j2) = (Re, Im)[F_c(j1) F_c(j2) conj(F_c(j1+j2))]/N. LP over laws w >= 0, sum w_c = 1: MINIMIZE the simple fraction sum_c w_c * #{i: m_i = 1}/N subject to (i) pair rows: |sum_c w_c S_c(j) - j/N| <= tau2 for 0 < j < N (edge row j = N free, replicating the 256-law setup); (ii) triple rows: |sum_c w_c A3_c(j1,j2) - t3(j1,j2)| <= tau3 for 1 <= j1 <= j2, j1 + j2 <= N, with t3 = 0 in the open simplex (the DS/CUE value; sanity-check t3 first by Monte Carlo over CUE samples at matrix size N). Solve by column generation: pricing = simulated annealing over (positions, marks) maximizing dual-weighted violation. OUTPUTS: p0^(2)(N) (baseline, should land near 0.68) and p0^(3)(N). READOUT: p0^(3) - p0^(2) > 0.02 => go (predicted range if binding: 0.69-0.73, anchored below the HL*(4) value 0.7222); < 0.005 => route refuted, publish as a no-go + run AH-structured configurations (positions on a half-integer lattice) to test whether they violate the triple rows at all. Also extract the pair-only dual (c0, r) at N = 128: candidate certificate for the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap. (B) INTERACTION MONTE CARLO for Lemma C. Build A-hat directly at d ~ 200 from the actual phihat evaluations: N_on on-line atoms (simples + doubles) at GUE-ish or adversarial spacings, plus n_p off-line pairs at depths y drawn from [0, 1/2] (u_rho with the X^{y} factors). Measure: tr A^3 vs sum m_j^3; the sizes of 3tr(P^2Q), 3tr(PQ^2), tr Q^3 as functions of depth and pair-pair offsets (the 'quadrupole' configurations that produced -4A^2 cancellations at order 2); verify odd-trace near-cancellation of deep pair blocks (predicted: tr Q^3 grows like the trace-ASYMMETRY, not like X^{3y}). This measures the remainder R in rank_trace_cubic before anyone tries to prove it, and directly tests the failure mode that killed per-pair pricing at order 2.
result.payoff: M1: exact price of the triple-correlation upgrade (a number, p0^(3)), the dual candidate certificates, and — either way it comes out — a publishable object: a higher ceiling with a road to it, or a formalized no-go extending the PairCeiling meta-theorem to order 3; plus the pair-only dual closing (or provably failing to close) the 0.0093 gap to 0.6818. M2: standalone headline theorem (first unconditional triple correlation for zeta), independent of the certificate program's fate; also upgrades the AH literature's data class. M3: breaks the lemmaR_tight invariant list — the first certificate format escape since the paper — with a formalizable matrix lemma contributed to RHLinalg. M4: new unconditional constants: any delta_d > 0 beats 5/6 (first improvement of Theorem C); delta_s > 0.0094 gives a certified simple-on-line proportion above the formalized bandwidth-one pair ceiling — a machine-checkable demonstration that the 0.6818287 wall is a property of the LINEAR class, not of bandwidth one; even a failed stretch goal yields the exact multilinear optimum. M5: two-sided (floor + ceiling) characterization of correlation order 3, the template for pricing every future correlation input before proving it. M6: potential refutation of the Alternative Hypothesis from provable-range data — which would be the most significant pair-correlation-adjacent result since Montgomery — and a quantified bridge toward 0.7222 without HL*(4).
result.thesis: Escape the formalized bandwidth-one pair ceiling without extending pair bandwidth, by proving the unconditional vanishing of the connected TRIPLE-correlation form factor of zeta zeros on the total-support-< 2 simplex (mixed-window trace tr(G_a G_b G_c), Rudnick-Sarnak range, de-conditionalized a la BGSTB) and consuming it through a cubic-integrality rank-trace certificate whose exact worth is computed first by adding triple rows to the 256-law extremal LP.
result.title: Breaking the pair ceiling from inside: unconditional mixed-window triple-correlation traces and a cubic rank-trace certificate

evades_obstructions.obstruction: DH/Epstein filter
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope, stated honestly: this is a proportion-improvement route (target 0.69-0.75, never RH). Bonus: the new input IS prime-specific anyway — the Selberg upper sieve for Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h) uses equidistribution of primes in arithmetic progressions (Euler-product/multiplicativity beyond L2-means). Davenport-Heilbronn coefficients violate it (their |c(n)|^2 grows like x^{1+delta} and no singular-series structure exists), so even the improved-proportion machinery does not extend to DH — consistent with the paper's Remark 7.2 observation that Prop 5.6 already fails for DH.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Alternative Hypothesis (bandwidth-1 pair correlation cannot distinguish GUE from half-integer spacing)
evades_obstructions.how: Not evaded — irrelevant. The certificate is a counting lower bound valid against EVERY configuration consistent with the data; it never needs to distinguish GUE from AH. Moreover the new band constraint F restricted to (1,1+eta] in [0, C_s] is strictly more than bandwidth-1 data, so the AH-indistinguishability theorem (arXiv:2507.06823) does not apply to the enlarged data class; we make no claim of ruling AH out.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bandwidth-one certificate ceiling 0.6818287 (formalized, PairCeiling)
evades_obstructions.how: Evaded by consuming bandwidth-(1+eta) data, which the formalized ceiling explicitly excludes from its scope (the Lean theorem covers certificates reading only the form-factor measure on [0,1]; the paper's own scope caveat lists 'bandwidth > 1' as outside). Concretely: the 256-law hides an atom of mass D(1)=0.824 exactly AT alpha=1, invisible to any r with r(1)=0; our sieve enclosure caps the smoothed form-factor mass on (1, 1+eta] by C_s*eta + o(1), which the banded LP (Milestone 0) uses to price how much of that atom is killed. The certificate value 2/3 + 2/(9 C_eff) exceeds 0.6818287 whenever the effective constant C_eff = C_s * A(omega) < 14.6 — the design's central quantitative gate, computed numerically before any proof effort.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: lemmaR_tight (two-moment rank-trace certificate exhausted)
evades_obstructions.how: Not contradicted: we do not improve the linear algebra. lemmaR_tight says the certificate is optimal GIVEN tr and ||.||_F^2 at bandwidth-one values; we change the value of ||.||_F^2 by feeding a smaller (bandwidth-1+eta, sieve-enclosed) second moment into the SAME tight inequality. The Lean k_c-form rank_trace_mult_k is already stated for arbitrary real weights, which is exactly what the omega-weighted compression produces.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Dimension cap d = lambda*N (nothing below lambda=1/2, 100% only at lambda=1)
evades_obstructions.how: Works in our favor: at lambda = 1.08-1.27 the cap is 108%-127% > our targets 0.69-0.75. The cap direction (certificate <= lambda*N) is slack throughout the proposed operating range.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: kappa(lambda) = 1/lambda + lambda/3 >= 2/sqrt(3): trace+Frobenius certificates cap at 0.8453 at ANY bandwidth
evades_obstructions.how: Respected: the horizon target 0.75 (full averaged-HL, C_s -> 1, lambda ~ 1.27) sits below 0.8453. The route's asymptote is the kappa-cap, honestly acknowledged; passing 0.8453 would need the fourth moment (HL* route, Milestone 5) or new invariants, not claimed here.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bombieri small-support Weil positivity unconditional (small cones prove nothing)
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope: we never argue W >= 0 on any cone. The mechanism is a counting certificate (lower bound on simple on-line zeros); Bombieri's theorem concerns proving positivity, which we neither need nor claim.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bombieri-Garrett ~94% pseudo-Laplacian spectral cap
evades_obstructions.how: Different architecture: no self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is claimed to contain zeros; the Gram compression is read only through inertia/trace/Frobenius. Our ceilings (kappa-cap 0.8453) are below 94% anyway.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Parity problem for sieve-only routes
evades_obstructions.how: Confronted head-on and priced: parity is exactly why C_s cannot be pushed to 1 by sieve alone (pointwise twin-prime upper bounds are stuck at 3.3996 >= 2, plausibly permanently >= 2). The design degrades gracefully in C_s: any finite C_s gives a positive bandwidth gain 2/(9 C_s A). Reaching the C_s -> 1 horizon requires h-averaged dispersion estimates (Lavrik/Mikawa-type, circle method, Deshouillers-Iwaniec), which are NOT sieve-only and hence not parity-blocked; the parity floor caps the sieve-only milestones at ~0.70-0.71, stated explicitly.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Conrey-Li counterexamples to de Branges positivity
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope: no de Branges space, no positivity condition of that type is used.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Rodgers-Tao Lambda >= 0 (no sub-critical margin)
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope: no heat-flow/de Bruijn-Newman deformation is used; the route makes no claim that would require a positive margin below criticality.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Campaign residue: 'every route's first substantive step was Weil positivity in disguise'; per-pair quadratic pricing FALSE; Pontryagin counting empty
evades_obstructions.how: The first substantive step here is (a) an elementary Fourier-analytic identity (smooth height weights annihilate the oscillatory off-diagonal — pure analysis, no positivity), and (b) a classical sieve upper bound on prime-pair correlations. Neither is Weil positivity in any disguise; the positivity certificate is the EXISTING Zeta23 machine, reused as a consumer. The new leverage is precisely the currency the campaign identified as missing: arithmetic input beyond bandwidth one (paper section 7.5(a) names HL-type prime-pair information as the sole obstruction; the overlooked gap is that a positivity certificate needs only a one-sided ENCLOSURE of O1, not its evaluation, and enclosure is unconditionally available from sieves). No per-pair quadratic pricing is used (mass-linear Lemma R only), and no negative-index counting.

failure_modes: C_eff too large: the effective band constant C_eff = C_s * A(omega) might exceed ~14.6 after honest bookkeeping of the kernel-envelope constant A(omega) (my derivation bounds it only up to an uncertainty-principle floor ~ 2*pi/(window width) with a factor-2 positive-part saving; the center-frequency phase e^{i c T theta} forces an absolute-envelope sandwich, and a sloppy envelope could cost another factor 2-3). Then the flat-window theorem lands between 2/3 and 0.6818 — new unconditional information at support 1+eta and a new theorem, but no ceiling breach. Mitigations, in order: enlarge the height-window aspect ratio K (A scales like 1/(K-1)), LP-optimal weight r from Milestone 0, Wu's 3.3996 for C_s, h-averaged sieve constants. Milestone 0 numerics decide this BEFORE proof investment.

The weighted Lemma-5.4 analogue (reduction of tr of the squared weighted Gram matrix to the double integral M_omega) may generate boundary/strip errors of size X*polylog that the smooth grid weights fail to absorb — the paper's version has error O(L*l*log l*(l^2+X)), lethal at X = T^{1+eta}; the claim that all such terms come from sharp k-truncation and die under smooth weights must survive line-by-line re-derivation. Fallback: run the certificate on a continuous-frame (integral) version of the compression where no grid truncation exists; inertia and the sampling identity both survive (Lean SeamMult layer is abstract enough).

Prior art: Goldston-Gonek (Mean values of long Dirichlet polynomials, 1998), Montgomery-Soundararajan, or a BGSTB follow-up (arXiv:2501.14545, 2603.28104, 2511.20059) may already contain the smoothed second moment of prime Dirichlet polynomials of length T^{1+eta} with sieve enclosure — the composition with a positivity certificate cannot predate Aug 2026, but the analytic core might; a literature pass is Milestone 0. All specific constants recalled from memory (Selberg's 4; Wu 2004's 3.3996; Mikawa's X^{1/3+eps} averaged-correlation threshold; Lavrik's average HL) are flagged for verification.

Sign/normalization error in the alpha-calibration of the resonant band (the (F(alpha)-alpha) accounting): my closed form H_1(lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - lambda/3 + (lambda-1)^3/(3 lambda^2) reproduces the paper's 1.043->0.70 and 1.265->0.80 price quotes with window optimization, which is strong but indirect evidence; the toy numeric (ratio 0.80 vs HL at T=4000) is consistent but small-scale. A factor-2 miscalibration halves the payoff. The Milestone-0 numeric at T=10^5-10^6 with three independent checks (zero-side vs prime-side vs model) catches this.

Ramp leakage on the zero side: partial-weight zeros on the omega-ramps charge k_2(u) = 4u - u^2 > 3u, and controlling this needs ramp width o(T) simultaneously with omega-hat decay (T*Delta)^{-A}; with ramp T/log T and C-infinity omega the constants c_A grow and must be tracked effectively — same class of difficulty the paper already handled for the taper phi (Prop 4.2), but a place where an o(1) could silently become O(1).

LP adversary: the banded-grid extremal law (Milestone 0) might exploit the freedom F in [0, C_s] on (1, 1+eta] plus a movable edge atom to pin the new ceiling barely above 0.6818, making the breach numerically real but unimpressively thin (e.g. 0.684). This would still refute 'bandwidth one is the wall' in principle but weaken the headline; the response is the K-aspect and fourth-moment levers.

Uniformity of the sieve bound under the specific smooth weights: the h-weight has slowly decaying tails (1+T|theta|)^{-A} and samples S(h) at scale h ~ n/T including the sliver n/T = O(1) where only h in {2,4,6} matter and S(h) spikes to O(loglog); shown to affect only an o(1) alpha-sliver, but the epsilon-management must be done honestly.
result.first_theorem: THEOREM (Sieve-enclosed smoothed second moment at bandwidth lambda = 1+eta). Fix lambda in (1, 6/5), a C^3 taper phi as in the Zeta23 paper with L = lambda*log(T/2pi), X = e^L = (T/2pi)^lambda, and a height weight omega in C_c^infinity((3/4, 9/4)), 0 <= omega <= 1, omega = 1 on [1,2], with ramp width 1/log T. Let G_omega := Omega^{1/2} G Omega^{1/2} be the omega-weighted Gabor-Gram matrix of the Weil form (Omega = diag(omega(tau_k/T))), in the paper's units. Then UNCONDITIONALLY, as T -> infinity: (a) [diagonal] tr G_omega-hat = N_omega (1+o(1)) with N_omega = sum_rho m_rho omega(gamma_rho/T); (b) [oscillation kill] the off-diagonal prime form restricted to |log(n/m)| > T^{epsilon}/T contributes O_A(T^{-A}) relative to the main term, for every A — a pure Fourier statement from omega-hat decay plus the aliasing-free Poisson identity (no arithmetic input beyond Chebyshev); (c) [sieve enclosure] the surviving resonant block R_omega = sum over prime-power pairs n != m <= X with |log(n/m)| <= T^{epsilon}/T of Lambda(n)Lambda(m)/sqrt(nm) * K_omega(n,m), K_omega(n,m) = 2*pi*g(log n)*T*(omega^2)-hat(T log(n/m)), satisfies |R_omega| <= (C_s + o(1)) * A(omega) * ((lambda-1)^2/(2 lambda)) * (main second-moment term), where C_s = 4 (Selberg upper sieve constant for sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h) <= (C_s+o(1)) S(h) X, uniform in 1 <= |h| <= X^{1-epsilon}) and A(omega) = integral |Re (omega^2)-hat(v)| dv / (2*pi* integral omega^2) is an explicit window constant; (d) [certificate] consequently ||G_omega-hat||_F^2 <= (1/lambda_1 + lambda_1/3 + C_s A(omega) (lambda-1)^2/(2 lambda_1) + o(1)) N, and via the real-weight rank-trace inequality (Lean rank_trace_mult_k), N_0^s(T,2T) >= (H_enc(lambda) - o(1)) N(T,2T) with H_enc(lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - lambda/3 - C_s A(omega) (lambda-1)^2/(2 lambda), whose maximum over lambda exceeds 2/3 by 2/(9 C_s A(omega)) > 0. STATUS OF INPUTS: the Selberg sieve bound is classical and proven (Halberstam-Richert; constant 4, improvable to 3.3996 by Wu 2004 — flagged for verification); the Poisson/aliasing infrastructure and the six-piece M[.,.] computation exist in the paper and Lean repo and need re-derivation with omega-weights (new but template-following); the weighted rank-trace assembly already exists leak-free for real weights in the Lean repo. ATTACK SKETCH: (1) prove the omega-weighted sampling identity with superpolynomially small aliasing (support of phi-hat*phi-hat is exactly [-L,L]; the omega(./T) modulation smears mass past the boundary only through T*omega-hat(T .)-convolution tails, giving O((wT)^{-1}-scale) leakage); (2) redo Prop 5.5-5.7 with omega-weights — all strip errors previously requiring pointwise |P_X| <= sqrt(X) bounds on sharp boundaries vanish because there is no sharp boundary; (3) split O1 at |theta| = T^{epsilon-1} and apply (b), then (c) with the termwise sandwich 0 <= sum_n Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h) <= C_s S(h) X against the absolute envelope of the kernel; (4) assemble via the k_c-form with real weights, paying O(N/log T) on the ramps. The referee-checkable core is (b)+(c): a statement about prime sums and explicit kernels, with no reference to zeta zeros.
