result.mechanism: OBJECT. The wall is formalized at Zeta23/PrimeSideB/PPOffDiag.lean:40 (O1_bound): the off-diagonal prime form O1 = sum_{n != m <= X} a_n a_m A^-(log n, log m), a_n = Lambda(n)/sqrt(n), is BOUNDED by 16 C (int Phi^2) sum Lambda(n)^2 ~ L^2 X via Montgomery-Vaughan, with zero cancellation used; this forces X <= T (lambda <= 1). Reading the paper's Prop 5.6 proof shows A^- is built from BOUNDARY evaluations of the inner integral int_I (n/m)^{i tau'} d tau' over the SHARP height window I = [T, 2T]: the 1/(y_n - y_m) kernel with phases (n/m)^{iT}, (n/m)^{2iT} is a sharp-cutoff artifact. THE TWO-STEP MECHANISM. Step 1 (oscillation kill — analysis only): replace the sharp Gabor-grid truncation k < d by smooth grid weights omega(tau_k/T), omega in C_c^infinity((3/4,9/4)), omega = 1 on [1,2], ramp 1/log T. The weighted Gram matrix G_omega = Omega^{1/2} G Omega^{1/2} preserves the entire zero-side architecture: P_omega >= 0 with rank <= rank P, n_+(Q_omega) <= n_+(Q) by inertia pull-back (congruence by a PSD diagonal), and the sampling identity gives each zero the real weight omega(gamma_rho/T) — consumed by the k_c-form rank_trace_mult_k which is already stated for arbitrary real weights. On the prime side the inner integral becomes int omega(tau'/T) omega((tau'+x)/T) (n/m)^{i tau'} d tau' = T*(omega^2)-hat(T theta)(1+O(L/T)), theta = log(n/m), which decays faster than any power of (1+T|theta|). Hence: all off-diagonal pairs with |theta| > T^{epsilon-1} contribute O_A(T^{-A}) — the entire Montgomery-Vaughan-bounded oscillatory mass, the O2 sum-frequency terms, and (crucially) the sharp-truncation strip errors of Lemma 5.4 that carry the other X-sized losses, are all annihilated. This is verified numerically: at T = 4000, X = T^{1.1}, the shoulder 40/T < |theta| <= 60/T contributes 10^{-18} of the diagonal. Step 2 (sieve enclosure — the new arithmetic input): the surviving RESONANT block is R_omega = sum_{n != m, |theta| <= T^{epsilon-1}} a_n a_m * 2 pi g(y_n) * T (omega^2)-hat(T theta), i.e. prime pairs n, n+h with 1 <= |h| <= n T^{epsilon-1} <= T^{eta+epsilon} — exactly the Hardy-Littlewood band that encodes the form factor F(alpha) on alpha in (1, lambda]. Its evaluation is HL-hard (the paper says so, section 7.5(a)) — but the CERTIFICATE consumes ||G-hat||_F^2 only through an UPPER bound, and the correlations are termwise NONNEGATIVE in h: 0 <= C_X(h) := sum_{n <= X} Lambda(n) Lambda(n+h) <= (C_s + o(1)) S(h) X unconditionally and uniformly in h (Selberg upper sieve, C_s = 4; Wu 2004 gives 3.3996 — flagged). So for the real kernel w(n,h) of R_omega: R_omega <= C_s * X * sum_h [w]_+ (h) S(h) (1+o(1)) and >= -C_s * X * sum_h [w]_- S(h): a two-sided enclosure with NO correlation asymptotics. CALIBRATION (checked two independent ways): in form-factor language the diagonal prime sum extended to X = T^lambda contributes 1/lambda + lambda/3 (the alpha-triangle with F-diagonal reading |alpha| on ALL of [0, lambda]), and the resonant block carries the correction int_1^lambda (1 - alpha/lambda)(F(alpha) - alpha) d alpha. Under exact HL (F = 1 past 1) this is NEGATIVE: the certificate becomes H_1(lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - lambda/3 + (lambda-1)^3/(3 lambda^2), and this closed form REPRODUCES THE PAPER'S PRICE LIST: H_1(1.043) = 0.6936, plus Montgomery-Taylor-type window re-optimization ~ +0.006 = 0.70; H_1(1.265) = 0.7917, + window ~ 0.80. Under the sieve enclosure the worst case in the band costs C_s A(omega) (lambda-1)^2/(2 lambda) with A(omega) = int |Re (omega^2)-hat| dv / (2 pi int omega^2) an explicit, optimizable window constant (the center-frequency phase e^{i c T theta} of the height window forces the absolute-envelope form; enlarging the height-window aspect ratio [T, KT] shrinks A like 1/(K-1)). CERTIFICATE VALUE: H_enc(lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - lambda/3 - C_s A(omega) (lambda-1)^2/(2 lambda) = 2/3 + (2/3) eta - (C_eff/2) eta^2 + O(eta^3), C_eff = C_s A(omega): maximized at eta* = 2/(3 C_eff) with GAIN 2/(9 C_eff) > 0 for ANY finite C_eff — every finite sieve constant buys a strictly positive bandwidth extension, because the marginal value of bandwidth at the edge is first-order ((2/3) eta from the 1/lambda + lambda/3 diagonal) while the price of ignorance in the band is second-order (eta^2, from the vanishing triangle weight at the edge). Beating the formalized 0.6818287 ceiling from the flat window requires C_eff <= 14.6; C_s = 4 with A(omega) <= 3.65 (or C_s = 3.4 with A <= 4.3, or aspect-ratio-enlarged windows) achieves it, and the LP-optimal certificate weight r (Milestone 0) plus Montgomery-Taylor window re-optimization add ~ +0.006 on top. Numerics at toy scale confirm the resonant block is real, HL-sized (ratio 0.80 to the S(h)-weighted prediction at T = 4000) and 5x inside the sieve envelope. WHY THE PAPER MISSED IT: section 7.5(a) frames the off-diagonal as needing EVALUATION ('Hardy-Littlewood asymptotics, equivalently PCC for alpha > 1'); the certificate needs only a one-sided ENCLOSURE, and one-sided prime-pair information of the right order is a 60-year-old sieve theorem. The oscillatory obstruction that made even enclosure look hopeless is a sharp-window artifact removable by smoothing that the fixed Gabor architecture concealed.
milestones: M0 (pricing + prior art, 1-2 months, numerics only): (i) Extend the exact-rational LP of PairCeiling/LawN256 to the banded grid j <= lambda*N with constraints 0 <= s_j <= C_s/N on the band (1,lambda] and an edge-atom variable at alpha = 1: compute the new ceiling v*(C_s, lambda) and the LP-OPTIMAL certificate weight r for C_s in {1, 2, 3.4, 4, 8} x lambda in {1.04, 1.08, 1.12, 1.2, 1.27}; confirm v*(4, 1.08) > 0.6818287 and quantify the D(1)=0.824 edge-atom kill. (ii) Optimize the window constant A(omega) over center/width/aspect-ratio/profile (explicit 1-d convex-ish search); determine achievable C_eff. (iii) Literature pass on Goldston-Gonek 1998, Montgomery-Soundararajan, Mikawa/Lavrik averaged correlations, and BGSTB follow-ups for prior art and to fix the recalled constants (Selberg 4, Wu 3.3996).

evades_obstructions.obstruction: DH/Epstein filter
evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope for full RH, and says so: the horizon goals are proportions, multiplicity-specific bounds (N_d, s_{2+}-mass), and refutation channels, never RH itself. Consistency check: for Davenport-Heilbronn the method self-destructs honestly - the prime-side mean-value step (Prop 5.6 analogue) fails because DH coefficients grow too fast, so both G and G' are uncomputable and the joint certificate is empty; for Epstein (class number >1) the same. Nothing in the mixed-moment route pretends to consume Euler-product-at-every-prime beyond L2 means, so no RH-completeness is claimed or implied.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Alternative Hypothesis (bandwidth-1 pair data cannot distinguish GUE from half-integer worlds)
evades_obstructions.how: The certificate no longer reads only xi pair-correlation data: tr(G G') is a CROSS correlation between xi-zeros and xi'-zeros, a data type outside the AH ambiguity class as formulated (AH concerns the single-object form factor). We do not claim to refute AH; but note the joint data is exactly the kind AH analysis has never constrained - an AH-consistent world must now also supply a derivative-zero configuration satisfying Rolle interlacing and derived-zero coincidences, a rigidity absent from pure pair-correlation modeling. Milestone 4 (joint ceiling LP) will determine quantitatively how much the link constraints shrink the adversary polytope.

evades_obstructions.how: Evaded by leaving the ceiling's data class, exactly along the escape route the formalization itself declares out of scope ('certificates reading only bandwidth-one [xi] form-factor data, configuration-by-configuration'). tr(G G') is not a functional of the xi form factor: the 256-periodic law has no xi'-layer, and no bandwidth-one xi-configuration data determines the cross moment. failure_modes: Signal-to-background failure: the forced coincident-atom contribution of one on-line multiple to tr(G_hat G_hat') is O(1) in N-units, but so is the generic (sine-kernel-level) xi.xi' clustering background; if the numerically measured ratio R is near 1, the joint LP gains ~0 and the program degrades to Milestone 1 (still a new unconditional theorem) plus Milestone 4 (a no-go).

Interference control: off-line-pair x off-line-pair cross terms in tr(GG') are signed and can be ~ -4A^2 (the quadrupole cancellation that killed termwise pricing); if the inertia-based regrouping cannot absorb them, the error budget eats the improvement eta. Mitigation is the paper's own pattern (never read the zero-side second moment termwise), but this is the main technical risk in Milestone 3.

Shallow-pair mimicry (known, structural): a depth 0+ pair with adjacent xi'-zeros is continuously indistinguishable from an on-line double, so s_1 (simple-on-line) may not improve at all; the honest expected gains are multiplicity-specific upper bounds (s_{2+}-mass, N - N_d) and the N_d ladder. If even these are blocked by adversary reallocation of free xi'-mass, only M1/M4 survive.

Mixed off-diagonal at lambda -> 1: the xi'-density prime term J carries log-corrections; if its off-diagonal bilinear form escapes the Montgomery-Vaughan absorption at the endpoint, the theorem holds only for lambda < lambda_0 < 1 with weaker constants (fallback stated in the first theorem).

WHY MULTIPLICITY BECOMES VISIBLE - THE TWO LINK CONSTRAINTS (exact algebra, not asymptotics): (L1) Derived zeros: if xi has a zero of multiplicity m >= 2 at rho (on OR off the line), xi' has a zero of multiplicity exactly m-1 at the SAME point, so the atom in G' sits on the SAME evaluation vector v_rho as the atom in G: P' >= sum_{multiples} (m_j - 1) v_j v_j^dagger in the PSD order, and each multiple FORCES a coincident-point contribution ~ m(m-1) |L Phi(0)|^2 to the mixed Fejer sum. An off-line pair of SIMPLE zeros forces neither. So the degenerate pair of lemmaR_tight (on-line double vs off-line pair, both charging 4 in the old certificate) splits: the double is FORCED to buy mixed-moment mass, the pair is not. CERTIFICATE. Apply the rank-trace machinery (rank_trace_mult_k, already stated for arbitrary real weights) to H_t = G_hat + t G_hat': on-line xi-points of multiplicity m carry weight >= m + t(m-1) (by L1, plus nonneg other xi'-mass), distinct on-line points cost rank 1, pairs of either object spend the n_+ budget; the three data values tr H_t = (1+t)N(1+o(1)), ||H_t||_F^2 = ||G_hat||_F^2 + 2t tr(G_hat G_hat') + t^2 ||G_hat'||_F^2 (all unconditionally computable - the cross term by the First Theorem, the outer two by the paper and by XiPrime), and the LP over integer multiplicities with charge k_c(m + t(m-1)) yield: an upper bound on the total multiplicity excess sum_rho (m_rho - 1) = N - N_d (both on- and off-line multiples are forced by L1 into the mixed moment), hence N_d >= (5/6 + eta)N; and an upper bound on the on-line multiple mass s_{2+} whenever the computed c_x is below the forced-coincidence threshold - the first multiplicity-specific (rather than distinctness-aggregate) unconditional bounds by any compression method. result.thesis: The de Branges kernel family E_a(z) = xi(a - iz) is not prime-computable at any fixed tilt a > 1/2, but its JETS in a at the critical tilt a = 1/2 are - the first jet is exactly a mixed xi.xi' explicit-formula form whose prime side is already formalized in Zeta23/XiPrime - and compressing the jet family yields a linked two-matrix certificate whose new invariant, the mixed moment tr(G G') plus the exact derived-zero constraint P' >= sum (m_j - 1) v_j v_j^dagger, is multiplicity-sensitive: precisely the invariant lemmaR_tight proves the current method lacks.
